title: Grant notification to beneficiaries
description: Tells a beneficiary that the grant has been made and what happens next.
guidance:
Write to a beneficiary of the estate. We act for the executors (or administrators), not for the beneficiary.

- Say that the Supreme Court has made the grant (probate or letters of administration, as the matter facts say), its date, and who it was granted to.
- Say briefly what happens next in general terms: the executors collect the estate's assets, pay its debts and expenses, and then distribute it under the will (or the intestacy rules).
- Don't promise when the beneficiary will be paid or how much they will receive. Say the executors will be in touch about timing once the estate's assets and debts are known.
- Ask the beneficiary to tell us of any change to their contact details.
- Suggest that they may wish to get their own legal advice about their entitlement, since we can't advise them.
